findings.element: Store card, row 2 "Created product should be: Inventory" helper text and "Open Settings" button
findings.finding: The card tells the user to switch the Synder setting from Non-inventory to Inventory without saying this changes how future synced sales post: Inventory-type items in QuickBooks Online require an Inventory Asset account, quantity on hand and an as-of date, and every sale of them posts Cost of Goods Sold.
findings.user_impact: A bookkeeper flipping the setting just to make stock sync work could start generating automatic Cost of Goods Sold and Inventory Asset entries in a client's books without intending to, changing margins and the balance sheet for every product Synder creates from then on.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one line of helper text with a Learn more link, e.g. "Products Synder creates in your books will be Inventory items, so their sales post Cost of Goods Sold", and keep the precise item-type terms rather than relabelling them.

evidence.quote: Now it is Non-inventory. Change it in Settings › My ceramic plates (Shopify) › Products/Services and click Update. This page updates by itself.
evidence.source: Accounting rule: QuickBooks Online Inventory items track quantity on hand and post Cost of Goods Sold / Inventory Asset on each sale; Non-inventory items do not. Domain scope: data integrity risk from a book-affecting change made without disclosure.

findings.element: Store card Mappings row and Sync warning ("won't sync")
findings.finding: "Sync" here means stock changes sent from QuickBooks to Shopify, but vocabulary.md defines Sync as sending data from Synder to the books, so "won't sync" reads as "this product's sales won't reach QuickBooks".
findings.user_impact: An accountant reading this as missing sales in the books may chase revenue that isn't missing, or remap items for the wrong reason, when only the Shopify stock count is affected.
findings.suggested_fix: Say what actually stops: "1 product has no QuickBooks item, so its stock changes won't be sent to Shopify."

evidence.quote: 1 product has no QuickBooks item and won't sync.
evidence.source: vocabulary.md line 104: "Sync (Synchronization) | post, push (syncing data from Synder to books)"; line 44: "Sync — synchronize to books. The main action."

findings.finding: The dialog promises a fixed total ("set to 140") but the feature sends a change (+8) computed at the last nightly comparison, so the total only holds if neither QuickBooks nor Shopify moved since 02:30 UTC.
findings.user_impact: A bookkeeper accepting hours after the comparison can end up with a Shopify count that still doesn't match QuickBooks while believing it was set to match, and the gap won't clear on its own.
findings.suggested_fix: Word it as a change: "Synder will send +8 to Shopify (difference at the last comparison, Oct 1, 2026 02:30 UTC). Click Compare now first if stock moved since."

evidence.quote: will be set to 140 (change +8). A sync event will be created to apply it.
evidence.source: Round context feature fact: "Synder … sends stock changes (not totals)"; "Accept QuickBooks" sends the difference. Reconciliation rule: an adjustment based on a stale comparison must be checked against current balances.

gaps: Settings › <integration> › Products/Services was never visited — the prototype sets Inventory instantly on Open Settings, so it is unknown whether the real settings page warns about the Cost of Goods Sold / Inventory Asset effect.
Mappings tab: the QuickBooks item select lists items without their type; it is unknown whether Non-inventory or Service items (which have no quantity on hand) can be mapped and what would be sent.
Accept QuickBooks was only exercised with no stock movement between comparison and accept, so the stale-difference outcome is unobserved.

The Reconcile "Shopify" column does not say which Shopify quantity it uses (On hand vs Available); unfulfilled orders could create false differences against QuickBooks Qty on hand, but no such sample exists in the state map.
No Failed sample events and Run now only toasts, so failure wording and the retry outcome for Failed changes could not be checked.
